svg.text: Electrowetting zig-zag column transport, computed with the force model

g.text: actuated contact line (rim over ON electrode)

svg.text: A. Asymmetric rim coverage lets one ON column pull every nearby droplet
Only the rim over the ON electrode is pulled, so the coverage imbalance is the net force.
One pulsed column captures droplets all along its length; their convergent motion drives coalescence.
B. Sequenced activation of progressively larger columns gives transport and size focusing
① next (larger) column ON, its tips capture the rim
② coverage grows, droplet funnelled and self-centred
③ parked (e⃗ ≈ 0); merged mass awaits the next, larger column
C. Size selectivity, where column spacing G selects the hand-off size
≥ hand-off size (R = 70 µm), rim spans the gap → captured
below hand-off (R = 38 µm), rim falls δ = 45 µm short → stranded

g.text: Hand-off radius R* vs column gap G (computed from the rim integral)

svg.text: → Spacing is the design knob. Gap G sets the hand-off radius R*, and droplets below R* must coalesce before they can advance.
